gap.methods: snpp / burned_area, base 2022; official / burned_area, base 2022
gap.direction: counts fell more than burned area
gap.timing_evidence: Punjab-wide only. Night share of S-NPP detections: 0.3% (95% interval 0.2% to 0.4%) in 2023 against 0.2% (0.1% to 0.2%) in 2022: supports a shift in timing. MODIS change relative to the S-NPP change since 2022: 1.18 times (rule: at least 1.5): does not support a shift in timing. MODIS passes at other times (Terra in the morning, Aqua drifting later in the afternoon), which is a confound.

caveat: The range shows only how the result changes with the count series and the base season. It does not include the error of the MODIS burned-area product, which is unknown and is the largest uncertainty. This is triangulation of satellite and official signals, not field verification.
explanations: A fall in detections per burned area fits three explanations: burning moved outside satellite pass times, fires became smaller or cooler, or the sensitivity of the burned-area product changed.
